newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NAB says Advance knows of NAB stake.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NAB says Advance knows of NAB stake.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd said on Thursday that Advance Australia Bank Ltd is fully aware that NAB has a 3.03 percent stake in Advance.

NAB managing director Don Argus said a statement by Advance earlier on Thursday to the effect that Advance did not know if NAB had bought five percent of Advance could be understood to imply that Advance had no knowledge of NAB's shareholding.

"To the extent that knowledge of National's holdings is material to the price of Advance shares, such implication could well mislead the market," Argus said in a letter to the Advance board released to the Australian Stock Exchange.
"As you are fully aware, National has a beneficial interest in shares of Advance. That holding is currently 3.03 percent of Advance's issued ordinary shares," Argus said in the letter.
An Advance spokesman earlier the bank was unaware of any purchases of its shares by NAB and was confident about the outcome of the proposed merger with St George Bank Ltd.
"We are not aware of any purchases by NAB," he said.

The Sydney Morning Herald reported on Thursday that Advance strongly suspected NAB had bought a stake of under five percent in order to agitate the A$2.65 billion takeover offer from St George at Advance's shareholder meeting on Monday.

NAB has an eight percent stake in St George and has blocked attempts to expand, buying converting preference shares in Metway Bank Ltd earlier this year to block St George's unsuccessful bid for the Brisbane-based bank.
NAB has said its St George stake is strategic, but many banking analysts see the stake as a launch-pad for a potential takeover bid if the St George-Advance deal does not go ahead.
Argus said NAB is considering all its options in deciding how to vote its shares, including abstaining from voting at the Advance meeting on Monday.

"Were National to decide to abstain from voting at that meeting and leave the fate of the proposed scheme in the hands of other Advance shareholders and the court, we would be very concerned with one aspect of the scheme, namely the deemed power of attorney device in clause 4 of the scheme," Argus's letter said.
The clause allows Advance directors to vote abstaining shares in favour of the proposal.
"National believes that this clause is unprecedented and ineffective in law," Argus said.

"Were National to abstain from voting at the scheme meeting, and were Advance to seek to exercise this so called power of attorney on behalf of National at the subsequent general meeting, National would not regard it as having any legitimate force or effect," Argus said.
"In such circumstances we would caution you against seeking to characterise our actions in any way other than as an abstention," he concluded.
Advance shares dropped and St. George shares climbed on Thursday on market speculation that the bid, regarded as overly generous to Advance shareholders, might be blocked by NAB.
St George shares rose 12 cents to A$7.80, after touching A$7.90 at one stage, and Advance closed six cents lower at A$6.75 after dipping to A$6.69.
